notes: Builder specialists for Tenonry. Copy verbatim to library/catalog.json. Field semantics: docs/03-COMPONENT-SPECS.md sections 3.2, 5.2, and 9.

specialists.title: CSS specialist
idioms: Express every color, spacing, radius, and type value through custom properties defined from the design direction tokens.
Use modern layout primitives (grid, flexbox, gap, clamp(), container queries) instead of fixed widths and margin hacks.
Keep selector specificity flat: single class selectors, no IDs, and no !important unless a comment explains why.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme wherever the design direction defines behavior for them.
slop: One border-radius and one soft grey shadow applied to every element regardless of hierarchy.
Hardcoded hex values and magic pixel numbers instead of tokens.
Fade-and-slide-up entrance animations on every section.

specialists.title: HTML and templates specialist
idioms: Use semantic elements (header, nav, main, section, article, button, label) before reaching for div and span.
Give every form control an associated label and every image meaningful alt text, or alt="" when decorative.
Keep one h1 per page and a logical heading order.
Keep logic out of templates: pass prepared data in and use partials or components for repetition.
slop: Clickable div elements instead of buttons and links.
Decorative eyebrow labels and numbered markers on content that is not a sequence.
Copy-pasted markup blocks instead of a partial or component.

specialists.title: React specialist
idioms: Write function components with hooks and derive values during render instead of syncing them into state with effects.
Keep components small and named for what users see; lift state only as far as the nearest common owner.
Use stable, data-derived keys for lists, never array indexes for data that can reorder.
Handle loading, empty, and error states explicitly for every async view.
slop: useEffect used to mirror props into state or to compute derived values.
useMemo and useCallback added everywhere without a measured reason.
Prop drilling through many layers, or one giant context holding unrelated state.

specialists.title: Next.js specialist
idioms: Default to Server Components and add "use client" only to the smallest interactive leaf.
Fetch data on the server close to where it is used and choose caching and revalidation deliberately.
Use next/image, next/font, and route-level loading and error files instead of hand-rolled equivalents.
Keep secrets in server-only modules and never import them into client components.
slop: "use client" at the top of every file.
Client-side fetching in useEffect for data the server could fetch.
API routes that only proxy data the page could read directly on the server.

specialists.title: Vue specialist
idioms: Use the Composition API with script setup and typed props and emits.
Use computed for derived state and watch only for side effects.
Extract reusable stateful logic into composables named useX.
Keep components presentational where possible and move shared state into Pinia stores.
slop: Watchers that copy one reactive value into another instead of a computed.
Mutating props directly.
Options API and Composition API mixed in one codebase without reason.

specialists.title: Angular specialist
idioms: Use standalone components, signals for local state, and inject() for dependencies.
Prefer OnPush change detection and the async pipe or signals over manual subscriptions.
Use the built-in template control flow (@if, @for with track).
Keep services focused and typed, with HTTP access in services rather than components.
slop: Manual subscribe calls in components without teardown.
Logic-heavy templates and functions called inside template bindings.
Shared god-services holding unrelated state.

specialists.title: Svelte and SvelteKit specialist
idioms: Use runes ($state, $derived, $effect, $props) and keep $effect for true side effects.
Load data in server load functions and use form actions for mutations.
Keep components small and pass data down with props; use stores or context only for shared state.
Build forms with progressive enhancement.
slop: $effect used to compute derived values.
Client-side fetch in onMount for data a load function should provide.
Global stores for state used by a single component.

specialists.title: SolidJS specialist
idioms: Use signals, memos, and resources, and never destructure props, which breaks reactivity.
Use Show, For, and Switch control-flow components instead of map calls and ternaries in JSX.
Keep effects for side effects only and derive values with createMemo.
slop: Destructured props that silently stop updating.
React patterns copied over, such as dependency arrays and useState-style setters everywhere.

specialists.title: Lit web components specialist
idioms: Declare typed reactive properties and keep internal state as private reactive state.
Scope styles with static styles and expose theming through CSS custom properties and ::part.
Dispatch typed custom events outward and accept complex data through properties, not attributes.
slop: Manual DOM manipulation inside render instead of declarative templates.
Global styles forced into shadow roots through workarounds.

specialists.title: Nuxt specialist
idioms: Fetch data with useFetch or useAsyncData so it is server-rendered and deduplicated.
Rely on auto-imports and file-based routing, and keep server-only code in server/.
Use useState or Pinia for shared state that must survive hydration.
Use runtime config for environment values, never hardcoded URLs.
slop: Plain fetch in onMounted for data that should be server-rendered.
Manual imports and router registration that fight Nuxt conventions.

specialists.title: Remix and React Router specialist
idioms: Load data in loaders and mutate in actions, reading results with the framework's data hooks.
Use Form and fetchers for mutations so pages keep working with progressive enhancement.
Return proper HTTP responses, status codes, and redirects from loaders and actions.
Handle failures with route error boundaries.
slop: Client-side useEffect fetching that duplicates a loader.
Manual form state and fetch calls where Form or a fetcher fits.

specialists.title: Astro specialist
idioms: Ship zero JavaScript by default and hydrate only interactive islands with the narrowest client directive.
Use content collections with schemas for structured content.
Use the built-in image component and static generation unless a page needs server rendering.
slop: client:load on every component.
Content kept as hardcoded arrays inside pages instead of collections.

specialists.title: Livewire specialist
idioms: Keep public properties minimal and typed, and authorize every action because users can tamper with public properties.
Choose wire:model modifiers (live, blur) deliberately and validate with rules.
Use computed properties for derived data and lazy loading for heavy components.
slop: wire:model.live on every input, causing a request per keystroke.
Authorization skipped in actions because the button is hidden in the view.

specialists.title: Alpine.js specialist
idioms: Keep x-data small and move reusable behavior into Alpine.data components.
Use Alpine.store for shared state and x-cloak to avoid flashes of unstyled content.
Keep accessibility attributes such as aria-expanded and focus management in sync with state.
slop: Large inline x-data objects duplicated across templates.
Toggles that change visibility without updating aria state.

specialists.title: htmx specialist
idioms: Return HTML fragments from the server and target the smallest element that changes.
Use hx-boost and progressive enhancement so links and forms work without JavaScript.
Use hx-indicator and proper HTTP status codes for loading and error states.
slop: JSON endpoints plus client-side templating that htmx makes unnecessary.
Swapping whole pages when one fragment changed.

specialists.title: jQuery and legacy JavaScript specialist
idioms: Use delegated event handlers on stable containers for dynamic content.
Cache selections and avoid repeated DOM queries inside loops.
Use native APIs (fetch, classList, querySelector) for new code when the file already does.
slop: Rewriting a legacy file in a new framework when the task asked for a fix.
New global variables and inline onclick handlers added to legacy pages.

specialists.title: Tailwind CSS specialist
idioms: Encode the design direction as theme tokens (the @theme block in v4 or the config theme) and use only those tokens in classes.
Extract repeated class groups into components rather than piling up @apply rules.
Use responsive, state, and dark variants consistently instead of custom media queries.
slop: Arbitrary values such as text-[13px] and bg-[#123456] instead of tokens.
The default palette and gradient washes used as decoration.
Identical rounded-xl shadow-md cards for every piece of content.

specialists.title: Sass specialist
idioms: Use the module system (@use and @forward), never @import.
Keep tokens in variables or maps and expose them as CSS custom properties.
Limit nesting to three levels and keep specificity flat.
slop: Deep nesting that mirrors the DOM structure.
Mixins and functions written for a single use.

specialists.title: CSS-in-JS specialist
idioms: Define a typed theme from the design direction tokens and read every value from it.
Declare styled components outside render functions, next to the component they style.
Use variants or props mapped to tokens instead of inline conditional style strings.
slop: Styled components created inside render and recreated on every render.
Hardcoded colors and spacing inside style literals.

specialists.title: TypeScript types specialist
idioms: Model domain data with precise types and discriminated unions, deriving related types instead of duplicating them.
Keep strict mode on and prefer unknown plus narrowing over any.
Export shared types from one place so frontend and backend agree on interfaces.
slop: any and type assertions used to silence errors.
Interfaces duplicated across files with slightly different fields.

specialists.title: Storybook specialist
idioms: Write stories in Component Story Format with args covering real states: default, loading, empty, error, and long content.
Apply the design direction tokens through decorators so stories render like production.
Add play-function interaction tests for interactive components when the project already uses them.
slop: A single default story per component that hides edge states.
Mock data that does not match the real data shapes.

specialists.title: React Native specialist
idioms: Use FlatList or FlashList for long lists, never a ScrollView with map.
Use StyleSheet.create with tokens, respect safe areas, and handle platform differences explicitly.
Give touch targets at least 44 by 44 points and add accessibilityLabel to icon buttons.
slop: Web-only CSS assumptions and fixed pixel layouts that break on other screen sizes.
Inline style objects recreated on every render throughout the app.

specialists.title: Flutter specialist
idioms: Compose small widgets and use const constructors wherever possible.
Stay consistent with the project's state management choice and keep business logic out of widgets.
Use Theme and ThemeExtension for tokens and never hardcode colors in widgets.
slop: Giant build methods with deeply nested widget trees.
setState used for app-wide state.

specialists.title: Electron specialist
idioms: Keep contextIsolation on and nodeIntegration off, exposing a minimal typed API through contextBridge in preload.
Validate every IPC message in the main process.
Keep the main process thin and move heavy work to utility processes or workers.
slop: nodeIntegration enabled to make a renderer feature work.
Generic IPC channels that accept any payload.

specialists.title: 3D and WebGL specialist
idioms: Use 3D only where the design direction calls for it, with a static fallback and respect for prefers-reduced-motion.
Lazy-load the scene and its assets after first paint so the main thread stays free during load.
Budget draw calls, texture sizes, and polygon counts; reuse geometries and materials and dispose resources on unmount.
Cap the device pixel ratio and pause rendering when the canvas is off-screen or the tab is hidden.
slop: A spinning hero object with no relation to the subject matter.
Uncompressed multi-megabyte models and textures loaded with the page.
Render loops running at full frame rate when nothing changes.

specialists.title: Laravel specialist
idioms: Validate input with Form Requests and authorize with policies or gates.
Keep controllers thin, put business logic in actions or services, and use dependency injection.
Use API Resources for response shapes, queued jobs for slow work, and config() rather than env() outside config files.
Use route model binding and named routes.
slop: Fat controllers with validation, queries, and formatting inline.
Repository interfaces wrapping Eloquent with a single implementation and no reason.
try/catch blocks that swallow exceptions the framework's handler would render correctly.

specialists.title: NestJS specialist
idioms: Organize code into feature modules with thin controllers and logic in providers.
Validate DTOs with class-validator and the global ValidationPipe.
Use guards for auth, interceptors for cross-cutting concerns, and exception filters for error shapes.
Inject configuration through ConfigService instead of reading process.env in services.
slop: Controllers containing business logic and database queries.
Generic base services and abstract repositories built for one entity.

specialists.title: Python specialist
idioms: Follow PEP 8 naming and add type hints to public functions.
Prefer small pure functions, dataclasses or pydantic models for structured data, and pathlib for paths.
Raise specific exceptions and handle them only where something useful can be done.
slop: Bare except clauses or broad except Exception blocks that hide failures.
Classes with one method that should be plain functions.

specialists.title: Django specialist
idioms: Keep views thin and put domain logic in model methods, managers, or service functions.
Validate with forms or DRF serializers and avoid N+1 queries with select_related and prefetch_related.
Read settings through the settings module and never hardcode secrets.
slop: Raw SQL where the ORM expresses the query clearly.
Business logic duplicated across views and serializers.

specialists.title: FastAPI specialist
idioms: Declare request and response models with pydantic and set response_model on routes.
Use Depends for auth, database sessions, and shared parameters.
Use async endpoints only with async libraries, and run blocking work in threads or background tasks.
slop: Blocking database or HTTP calls inside async def endpoints.
Plain dicts returned instead of typed response models.

specialists.title: Flask specialist
idioms: Use the application factory pattern and one blueprint per feature.
Validate input explicitly and return consistent JSON errors.
Load configuration from the environment into config classes.
slop: A single app.py containing every route.
Global mutable state shared across requests.

specialists.title: Node.js specialist
idioms: Use ES modules and async/await, and never block the event loop with synchronous I/O in request paths.
Validate external input at the boundary and handle every promise rejection.
Read configuration once at startup from the environment and pass it down.
slop: Unhandled rejections and floating promises.
Callback and promise styles mixed in the same module.

specialists.title: Express specialist
idioms: Structure routers per resource with thin handlers that delegate to services.
Validate requests with a schema library such as zod or joi in middleware.
Use one centralized error-handling middleware and forward async errors to it.
Set security headers and limit request body size.
slop: try/catch in every handler that responds with a generic 500.
Business logic inside route callbacks.

specialists.title: Fastify specialist
idioms: Declare JSON schemas for body, params, and responses so validation and serialization are automatic.
Encapsulate features as plugins and share services through decorators.
Use hooks such as onRequest and preHandler for auth and cross-cutting logic.
slop: Routes without schemas.
Express-style middleware patterns forced into Fastify.

specialists.title: Hono specialist
idioms: Group routes with app.route per feature and type the environment bindings.
Validate input with validator middleware such as zod-validator and return typed responses.
Keep code runtime-agnostic unless the project targets a single runtime.
slop: Node-only APIs used in code meant for edge runtimes.
Untyped context variables passed around as any.

specialists.title: Deno specialist
idioms: Use explicit permissions and the standard library, managing imports through the import map in deno.json.
Use Deno.serve and web-standard Request and Response APIs.
Follow deno fmt, deno lint, and deno check conventions.
slop: Node compatibility shims where a Deno or web-standard API exists.
Remote imports from unversioned URLs.

specialists.title: Symfony specialist
idioms: Use autowired services, attribute routing, and constructor injection.
Validate DTOs with the Validator component and authorize with Voters.
Keep controllers thin and use Messenger for asynchronous work.
slop: Fetching services from the container directly.
Controllers holding business logic and Doctrine queries.

specialists.title: PHP specialist
idioms: Use declare(strict_types=1), typed properties, and return types.
Follow PSR-12 style and PSR-4 autoloading, using constructor property promotion and readonly where they fit.
Throw specific exceptions and never suppress errors with @.
slop: Arrays used as untyped data structures where a small class or enum fits.
Static helper classes accumulating unrelated functions.

specialists.title: Go specialist
idioms: Return errors, wrap them with context using fmt.Errorf and %w, and handle each error once.
Accept interfaces and return structs, defining interfaces at the consumer.
Pass context.Context first for request-scoped work and respect cancellation.
Keep packages small and named for what they provide.
slop: Interfaces declared next to their only implementation.
panic used for ordinary errors.
Getters and setters on every struct field.

specialists.title: Rust (Axum) specialist
idioms: Use extractors for input, typed State for shared dependencies, and IntoResponse for error types.
Model errors as enums (for example with thiserror) and propagate them with ?, avoiding unwrap and expect outside tests.
Borrow instead of cloning where lifetimes stay simple, and keep async code free of blocking calls.
slop: clone() added just to satisfy the borrow checker.
unwrap() in request paths.

specialists.title: Spring Boot specialist
idioms: Use constructor injection, records for DTOs, and Bean Validation on request bodies.
Keep controllers thin and put transactions on service methods.
Handle errors centrally with @ControllerAdvice and problem details.
slop: Field injection with @Autowired.
JPA entities exposed directly as API responses.

specialists.title: Kotlin (Ktor) specialist
idioms: Organize routes as extension functions per feature and install plugins for serialization, auth, and status pages.
Use data classes for DTOs with kotlinx.serialization.
Write suspend functions correctly and never block inside handlers.
slop: runBlocking inside request handlers.
Nullable values forced with !! instead of handled.

specialists.title: ASP.NET Core specialist
idioms: Use dependency injection with appropriate lifetimes and the options pattern for configuration.
Validate input, return ProblemDetails for errors, and stay async all the way through.
Keep endpoints thin, whether minimal APIs or controllers, with logic in services.
slop: Async methods blocked with .Result or .Wait().
Service locator calls instead of constructor injection.

specialists.title: Ruby on Rails specialist
idioms: Follow Rails conventions: RESTful resources, strong parameters, and validations in models.
Avoid N+1 queries with includes and use scopes for reusable queries.
Move complex domain logic into plain Ruby objects and slow work into background jobs.
slop: Callbacks that hide side effects such as emails and API calls.
Service objects wrapping one-line operations.

specialists.title: Elixir Phoenix specialist
idioms: Keep business logic in contexts, with controllers and LiveViews calling context functions.
Validate with Ecto changesets and express control flow with pattern matching.
Use function components and keep LiveView socket assigns minimal.
slop: Repo calls made directly from controllers or LiveViews.
Defensive nil checks where pattern matching expresses the cases.

specialists.title: GraphQL specialist
idioms: Design the schema around client use cases and choose nullability deliberately.
Batch data loading with DataLoader to avoid N+1 resolvers.
Enforce authorization in resolvers or a shared layer, and limit query depth and cost.
slop: Schemas that mirror database tables one to one.
Resolvers that query the database once per item.

specialists.title: gRPC and Protobuf specialist
idioms: Design messages for evolution: never reuse field numbers and reserve removed ones.
Set deadlines, return proper status codes, and keep services small and cohesive.
Keep generated code out of hand-written directories.
slop: Generated stubs edited by hand.
Field numbers or types of existing fields changed.

specialists.title: Serverless functions specialist
idioms: Keep handlers thin and initialize clients outside the handler so invocations reuse them.
Make handlers idempotent and set timeouts and memory deliberately.
Grant least-privilege permissions per function.
slop: Wildcard IAM permissions.
Heavy initialization inside the handler on every invocation.

specialists.title: PostgreSQL specialist
idioms: Write reversible migrations that are safe on large tables: add columns nullable, backfill, then constrain, and create indexes concurrently.
Enforce invariants with NOT NULL, foreign keys, CHECK, and UNIQUE constraints.
Index for the real query patterns and confirm with EXPLAIN.
Parameterize every query.
slop: SELECT * in application queries.
An index added on every column.

specialists.title: Prisma specialist
idioms: Model relations explicitly with referential actions and add @@index for real query patterns.
Create migrations with prisma migrate and never edit applied migrations.
Select only the fields needed and wrap multi-step writes in transactions.
slop: Hand-edited applied migration files.
Whole relation trees fetched with include where select would do.

specialists.title: MySQL and MariaDB specialist
idioms: Use InnoDB, utf8mb4, and explicit foreign keys and indexes.
Write migrations that stay online-safe on large tables.
Parameterize every query.
slop: Implicit type conversions in WHERE clauses that defeat indexes.
Booleans and enumerations stored as free-form strings.

specialists.title: SQLite specialist
idioms: Enable foreign keys and WAL mode where the project controls connections.
Keep transactions short and batch writes inside a single transaction.
Account for type affinity by enforcing types with CHECK constraints or STRICT tables.
slop: A new connection opened for every query.
Assuming concurrent writers scale like a server database.

specialists.title: SQL Server specialist
idioms: Use parameterized queries and deliberate types such as datetime2 and sized nvarchar columns.
Index for the real query patterns and check execution plans.
Use explicit transactions with suitable isolation levels.
slop: nvarchar(max) for every string column.
Cursors where a set-based query works.

specialists.title: MongoDB specialist
idioms: Design documents around access patterns: embed what is read together and reference what grows without bound.
Define an index for every query pattern and validate documents with Mongoose or JSON Schema.
Use projections and lean queries for reads.
slop: Relational-style normalization requiring many lookups.
Arrays that grow without bound inside documents.

specialists.title: Redis specialist
idioms: Namespace keys consistently and set TTLs on cache entries.
Choose the fitting data structure (hash, set, sorted set, stream) instead of serialized blobs.
Handle cache misses and stampedes, and never treat Redis as the only copy of durable data unless it is configured for that.
slop: Cache keys without expiry.
The KEYS command used in application code.

specialists.title: DynamoDB specialist
idioms: Design keys from access patterns first and add secondary indexes deliberately.
Use Query instead of Scan, and conditional writes for consistency.
Keep items small and use batch operations where they fit.
slop: Scan used for lookups.
Relational modeling with many tables joined in application code.

specialists.title: Azure Cosmos DB specialist
idioms: Choose high-cardinality partition keys that match the main query patterns.
Keep hot-path queries within one partition and watch request unit cost.
Use one SDK client instance for the application's lifetime.
slop: Cross-partition queries on hot paths.
A new client created per request.

specialists.title: Elasticsearch and OpenSearch specialist
idioms: Define explicit mappings instead of relying on dynamic mapping in production.
Index with the bulk API and use aliases for zero-downtime reindexing.
Use filter context for exact matches and query context for relevance scoring.
slop: Dynamic mapping turning every field into text plus keyword.
Deep pagination with from and size.

specialists.title: ClickHouse specialist
idioms: Choose ORDER BY keys for the main filters and the right MergeTree engine.
Insert in large batches rather than row by row.
Use materialized views for pre-aggregation.
slop: Frequent small inserts.
Updates and deletes used as if ClickHouse were an OLTP database.

specialists.title: Snowflake specialist
idioms: Write set-based SQL and size warehouses deliberately instead of processing row by row.
Add clustering keys only for very large tables with clear filter patterns.
Use least-privilege roles and avoid SELECT * on wide tables.
slop: Python loops over query results that SQL could aggregate.
Credentials hardcoded in connection code.

specialists.title: Drizzle ORM specialist
idioms: Define the schema in TypeScript with explicit relations, indexes, and constraints.
Generate migrations with drizzle-kit and review them before applying.
Use the typed query builder with explicit selects and wrap multi-step writes in transactions.
slop: Raw SQL strings where the typed builder expresses the query.
Drift between schema files and migrations.

specialists.title: TypeORM specialist
idioms: Use explicit migrations and never enable synchronize in production.
Define relations with explicit join columns and indexes.
Use QueryBuilder or find options with select to avoid loading whole graphs.
slop: synchronize: true outside local development.
Eager relations everywhere.

specialists.title: Sequelize specialist
idioms: Use migrations for every schema change and define associations in one place.
Choose attributes and include deliberately to avoid over-fetching.
Wrap multi-step writes in transactions.
slop: sequelize.sync({ alter: true }) run at application startup.
Raw queries built with string interpolation.

specialists.title: Eloquent and Laravel database specialist
idioms: Define relationships, casts, and $fillable deliberately, and never allow mass assignment of ownership fields.
Write migrations with foreign keys, indexes, and down methods, and use factories and seeders for test data.
Prevent N+1 queries with eager loading and use query scopes for reusable constraints.
slop: $guarded = [] on models.
Raw DB queries where Eloquent or the query builder expresses the query clearly.

specialists.title: Doctrine ORM specialist
idioms: Map entities with attributes, keep invariants inside entity methods, and put queries in repositories.
Generate migrations with Doctrine Migrations and review them.
Avoid N+1 queries with fetch joins in DQL.
slop: Anemic entities with a public setter for every field.
flush() called inside loops.

specialists.title: SQLAlchemy and Alembic specialist
idioms: Use SQLAlchemy 2.0 style with typed Mapped columns and select() statements.
Manage one session per unit of work and generate migrations with Alembic autogenerate, then review them.
Use selectinload or joinedload deliberately to avoid N+1 queries.
slop: A global session shared across requests.
Autogenerated migrations committed without review.

specialists.title: Django ORM specialist
idioms: Declare constraints and indexes in Meta and use TextChoices or IntegerChoices for enumerations.
Create migrations with makemigrations and keep data migrations separate from schema migrations.
Put reusable query logic in custom managers and querysets.
slop: Applied migrations edited by hand.
Queries inside loops instead of select_related or prefetch_related.

specialists.title: dbt specialist
idioms: Layer models into staging, intermediate, and marts, referencing them with ref() and source().
Document and test models in schema YAML with unique, not_null, and relationships tests.
Use incremental models for large tables with a clear unique key.
slop: Hardcoded table names instead of ref() and source().
One giant model doing every transformation.

specialists.title: PySpark and AWS Glue specialist
idioms: Use DataFrame operations and built-in functions instead of Python UDFs where possible.
Partition outputs by query patterns and avoid producing many small files.
Make jobs idempotent and parameterized, using job bookmarks for incremental loads.
slop: collect() or toPandas() on large datasets.
Python UDFs for operations Spark already provides.

specialists.title: Vector store specialist
idioms: Store the embedding model name and dimension with the data and keep them consistent.
Chunk documents deliberately, with overlap and metadata for filtering.
Use metadata filters and suitable index types, and batch upserts.
slop: Re-embedding the whole corpus on every change.
Embeddings from different models mixed in one index.
